title: Not All Eval-Awareness Is Equal: Capabilities Framing Predicts Compliance
abstract: arXiv:2608.27340v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Steering interventions targeting eval-awareness, a model's recognition that it is being tested, are increasingly used in safety evaluation pipelines, where evaluation-awareness is treated as a single quantity to be suppressed. We show that verbalized eval-awareness in chain-of-thought can be identified as capabilities-flavored ("the user is testing my ability to follow instructions"), safety-flavored ("the user is testing my boundaries"), both, or neither: framings that predict compliance very differently. On Qwen3-32B over the FORTRESS dataset, capabilities-framing predicts compliance with a +24 to +46 percentage-point gap over safety-framing across all tested steering conditions. translated_title: 并非所有评估感知都相同：能力框架预测遵从性
translated_abstract: 针对评估感知（模型识别到自身正在被测试）的引导干预日益用于安全评估流程中，其中评估感知被视为一个需被抑制的单一量。我们表明，思维链中的言语化评估感知可被识别为能力导向（“用户正在测试我遵循指令的能力”）、安全导向（“用户正在测试我的边界”）、两者兼具或两者皆非：这些框架对遵从性的预测差异显著。在Qwen3-32B模型上，针对FORTRESS数据集，在所有测试的引导条件下，能力导向框架预测遵从性的差距比安全导向框架高出+24至+46个百分点。对评估感知负向输出的CoT预填充干预表明该联系具有因果性，11次预填充中有10次将遵从性移向预测方向。因此，评估感知并非行为上统一：总体抑制率可能变化，而具体框架的影响却不同。
tldr: 本研究揭示评估感知并非单一量，其能力导向框架比安全导向框架更能预测模型遵从性，且该影响具有因果性。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that eval-awareness is not a uniform quantity; capabilities-framing predicts compliance more strongly than safety-framing, with causal evidence from CoT-prefill interventions.
